chunks: My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abu Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abd Allah (AS) who said:

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made Ibrahim (AS) and Sarah feed the children of the believers from a tree in Paradise which has udders like the udders of cows, in palaces made of pearls. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be dressed, perfumed, and presented to their parents, so they and their parents will be kings in Paradise.
ai.seo_question: How are the children of believers provided for in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to illustrate Allah’s justice in compensating for the premature death of children, emphasizing their eternal status as 'kings' alongside their parents. The specific detail of nourishment from a tree with 'cow-like leaves' highlights the unique, abundant sustenance provided by Ibrahim and Sarah, reinforcing the concept of familial reunion and elevated rank in Jannah.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of al-Haytham ibn Abu Masruq al-Nahdi, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ri`ab, on the authority of al-Halabi that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said,

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made Ibrahim and Sarah feed the children of the believers from the tree in Paradise, which has udder like the udder of a cow. They are in palaces made from pearls. When the Day of Judgement comes, they will be dressed up, perfumed, and brought to their parents. Both the children and their parents will be royalty in Paradise.
